summary: Bradford Lyman Phillips specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Naropa University, earned a B.A. and Ph.D. at the University of Virginia, and an M.T.S. at Harvard, working under David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling works in religious studies and philosophy. He served as Assistant Director at Boston University and held a post at Marymount Manhattan College (attested 2008).

Braj Basi Lal was an Indian archaeologist and Indologist. He earned a master's in Sanskrit from the University of Allahabad and trained under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the ASI, department head at Jiwaji University, and Director of IIAS.

Brandon Dotson is a scholar of Tibetology and archaeology. He earned his D.Phil. under Charles Ramble at Oxford and completed his habilitation at the University of Munich. His posts include positions at SOAS, Munich, and the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences.

Brandon J. Harwood works in philosophy and religious studies. He completed his Ph.D. at the University of Louisville under Patrick Pranke and served there as Project Coordinator and Senior Lecturer in 2018.

Bratindra Nath Mukherjee was an Indologist and historian. He earned degrees from the University of Calcutta and SOAS (under A. L. Basham), and also studied at Cambridge. He was Carmichael Professor of Ancient Indian History and Culture at Calcutta (1975–1998).

Brendan Ozawa-de Silva specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned a D.Phil. from Oxford and a Ph.D. from Emory. He has taught as an Associate Professor at Life University and an Associate Teaching Professor at Emory.

Brendan S. Gillon works in linguistics, Indology, and philosophy. Educated at MIT, he has served as an Associate Professor of Linguistics at McGill University and Professor of Sanskrit and Linguistics at the University of Michigan (2012–2014).

Bret W. Davis works in philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He earned a B.A. from Vanderbilt and studied at Kyoto University. His academic career includes faculty posts at Loyola University Maryland, Shiga, Kwansei Gakuin, and fellowships at Otani and Kyoto.

Brian A. Hatcher is a scholar in religious studies and Indology. His academic career includes appointments in the Department of Religion at Illinois Wesleyan University (attested 1995) and at Elon University (attested 1996).
Brian Bocking is a scholar in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Michael Pye and earned his Ph.D. from the University of Leeds (attested 1984).
Brian Cutillo worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology from roughly 1963 to 1967 and was a student of Geshe Wangyal.

Brian D. Ruppert is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies mentored by Willis Stoesz. He held posts at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1999–2018) and Bates College (~2018) as Kazushige Hirasawa Professor.

Brian Daizen Victoria works in Buddhist studies and Japanology. Educated at Komazawa, Temple, and Eihei-ji, he held posts at Antioch, Adelaide, Auckland, and Hawaiʻi, as well as fellowships at the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies and Nichibunken.

Brian Gregory Baumann specializes in Central Asian history and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. at Indiana University Bloomington under György Kara and serves as a Mongolian language lecturer at UC Berkeley and the Numata Center.

Brian Houghton Hodgson was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. Educated at East India Company College and Fort William College, he served as the British Resident and Assistant Resident at the Court of Nepal between 1820 and 1843.

Brian J. Nichols specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at the Inter-University Program for Chinese Language Studies and earned his Ph.D. at Rice University (attested 2011) under Anne Carolyn Klein.

Bridget Allchin was an archaeologist and Indologist. She studied at the University of Cape Town and earned her Ph.D. at UCL. A Wolfson College Fellow, she co-founded the Ancient India and Iran Trust and the European Association of South Asian Studies.
Brigitte Marschall earned her doctorate at the University of Vienna (1980–1984) and later served there as an associate professor (außerordentliche Universitätsprofessorin) starting around 1997.
Brigitte Steinmann is a scholar in Tibetology who studied under Alexander W. Macdonald and Bahadur Singh. She held a post at the University of Montpellier (attested 2004).
